To learn Python for AI, focus on variables, data types, conditions, loops, functions, lists, dictionaries, file handling, OOP, modules, and small automation projects.
For machine learning, learn supervised learning, regression, classification, model evaluation, overfitting, feature engineering, and scikit-learn projects.
For deep learning, start with neural networks, backpropagation basics, CNNs, RNNs, transformers, PyTorch or TensorFlow, and then build image and text-based projects.
For NLP, start with text preprocessing, tokenization, bag-of-words, TF-IDF, sentiment analysis, text classification, embeddings, transformers, and then RAG.
For computer vision, start with OpenCV, image preprocessing, CNNs, image classification, object detection, transfer learning, and real-time camera-based projects.
RAG means Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Learn document loading, chunking, embeddings, vector databases, retrieval, prompt design, and LLM-based answer generation.
For LLM fine-tuning, first understand datasets, tokenization, instruction tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, evaluation, GPU limits, and when fine-tuning is better than RAG.
AI agents use LLMs with tools, memory, planning, and actions. Start by building a simple tool-using assistant, then add memory, task planning, and external APIs.
To deploy an AI/ML app, create a FastAPI backend, expose prediction or chat endpoints, test locally, add Docker, and deploy on Render, Railway, AWS, GCP, or Azure.
Good AI portfolio projects include: AI Career Mentor Bot, sentiment analyzer, ML prediction API, resume screening bot, RAG PDF chatbot, computer vision attendance system, and AI agent assistant.
For AI career growth, build strong GitHub projects, write clear READMEs, deploy at least one app, add project demos, improve LinkedIn, and explain your work through case studies.
